title: When Everyone Adopts the Same Channel, the Advantage Disappears
content:
###  **A Documented Example** 

Google Local Services Ads offer a clear illustration of a pattern most contractors have experienced without seeing it measured. 

Contractor adoption of Local Services Ads rose from roughly 28 percent in 2021 to approximately 70 percent by 2026. What gave early adopters a real edge is now closer to a requirement — the cost of not participating, rather than an advantage from participating. 

###  **The Pattern Underneath** 

Nearly every marketing channel follows the same arc. It works unusually well when few companies use it. As adoption spreads, results normalize. Eventually it becomes something you have to do to stay level, without producing any separation from competitors. 

None of this means a mature channel is worthless. Local Services Ads still produce jobs. But a channel at 70 percent adoption is not where a company finds an edge. 

###  **Where the Advantage Actually Sits** 

Advantage tends to live in whatever most competitors have not adopted — usually because it requires effort they would rather avoid. 

Structured neighborhood conversation is a reasonable example. It cannot be switched on with a credit card. It requires finding people who are genuinely good at talking to strangers, training them, supervising them, and doing it consistently for months. That difficulty is precisely why adoption stays low, and precisely why it still produces separation. 

###  **The Honest Caveat** 

This is not an argument for abandoning mature channels. A contractor who drops Local Services Ads because everyone uses them will simply lose the jobs those ads produce. 

It is an argument about where incremental budget goes. Adding more spend to a saturated channel buys roughly what competitors are buying. Adding a channel most of them have not adopted buys something they do not have. 

###  **The Question Worth Asking Annually** 

Of the channels currently in your marketing mix, how many would a competitor down the road be able to replicate by the end of next week? 

Whatever is left after that question is where the actual advantage lives.
